name: Sinocentrism
summary: Sinocentrism treats China as the cultural and political centre of the world, ruled by an emperor who as Son of Heaven holds the Mandate of Heaven over all under heaven. Civilisation is measured by Confucian morality and ritual, so outsiders are ranked as more or less barbarian and are expected to show deference through tribute and investiture while adopting Chinese ways. Trade and diplomacy are conducted on the centre's terms, and foreign manufactures and institutions are held to be unnecessary or unsuitable for China.
scope: The imperial worldview of the Ming and Qing courts, illustrated by Qianlong's 1793 letter to George III and by Confucian political thought, with the Hua-Yi distinction and tributary system as its institutions. Modern tianxia revivalism and Chinese nationalism are noted in the notes but not the basis of the answers; most answers on modern economic, social and technological questions are inferred and rated low.

keyFigures.name: Qianlong Emperor
keyFigures.role: Qing emperor whose 1793 letter to George III states the Sinocentric view of tribute and trade.

keyFigures.name: Confucius
keyFigures.role: Thinker whose moral and ritual order defined the civilisation by which Sinocentrism ranked peoples.

keyFigures.name: Zhao Tingyang
keyFigures.role: Philosopher whose tianxia theory is the best-known modern revival of the idea.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Imperial Sinocentrism had no doctrine on health provision; paternalist benevolence of the ruler points mildly toward it but adherents would not frame it as a state entitlement.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage regulation is foreign to the imperial worldview; Confucian care for the people is the only loose guide, and it gives no clear direction.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Qianlong treats trade as a court-licensed favour confined to Canton, so adherents do not credit free markets, though the Confucian state also did not plan production.

public-ownership.rationale: The imperial state held salt and iron monopolies at times, but Sinocentrism as a worldview is silent on utilities; inferred as split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Confucian thought favours light taxation of the people and moral restraint of the rich rather than redistributive taxes; the worldview does not settle it.

unions-good.rationale: Autonomous organised bodies outside the hierarchy of ruler, officials and family sit badly with Confucian order; inferred from its stress on hierarchy.

property-fundamental.rationale: Imperial China recognised private landholding but all land was ultimately the emperor's under Heaven; adherents are not committed either way.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Commerce was supervised by the court as in the Canton system, but corporations as such are anachronistic; no stated position.

cut-welfare.rationale: Confucian benevolent rule expects the ruler to relieve the destitute, so cutting relief runs against it; inferred, not a Sinocentric doctrine itself.

worker-ownership.rationale: Nothing in the imperial order supports collective worker control, which would cut across hierarchy; inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Imperial government monitored its subjects and foreigners closely (Qianlong notes restrictions on Europeans in the capital), so state security surveillance is unproblematic; inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Moral cultivation is central to Confucian governance, so permissiveness on drugs is disfavoured; inferred, and the Qing did try to ban opium.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The question is anachronistic; the worldview itself calls foreigners barbarians, yet the state also valued moral order in speech.

strong-leader.rationale: The emperor as Son of Heaven was meant to hold supreme authority, with virtue rather than gridlock-breaking as the stated ground; leadership by a single paramount ruler is core.

state-harmful.rationale: Confucian-imperial doctrine treats the state under a virtuous ruler as the necessary moral order of civilisation, the opposite of anarchism.

limit-guns.rationale: Imperial rule monopolised armed force and favoured order, so strict control is consistent; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Force defended and expanded the system, but Confucian doctrine ranks moral example above coercion, so adherents are split.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Confucian moral order and family ethics disfavour it; inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: The model is a centre radiating authority outward, with unified rule from the court, so decentralisation to the lowest level is not its aim.

rehabilitation.rationale: Confucian preference for moral transformation suits rehabilitation, but the imperial order also used harsh punishment; split.

traditional-family.rationale: Family relationships and filial piety are the base of Confucian social order, which Sinocentric civilisation claims as its own.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not an issue in the tradition; its family-centred lineage ethics point against it, inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: Lineage continuity and family duty weigh against it, though not explicitly addressed; inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Qianlong dismisses Christianity as a heterodox doctrine, yet Confucian state ritual is itself public; adherents favour the Confucian moral order, not religion broadly.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The Hua-Yi hierarchy ranks peoples by civilisation, so adherents would not frame policy around correcting racial injustice; inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Confucian ethics assign men and women distinct roles as natural to the five relationships; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Chinese civilisation and Confucian propriety are the measure of all culture; preserving them is central.

gradual-change.rationale: Confucian ethics prize established ritual and institutions and dynastic continuity; Qianlong refuses innovations as contrary to custom.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Qianlong restricts foreigners to Canton and refuses resident envoys; entry of outsiders is tightly limited.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Sinocentrism envisions order centred on China, not equal-voting bodies; tianxia revivals criticise the Western order.

free-trade.rationale: Qianlong declares China has no need for foreign manufactures and limits trade to Canton; trade is a court-regulated favour.

nation-first.rationale: The empire sets its own interests and customs above outside demands, as in the refusal of British requests.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Imperial China was typically non-interventionist toward tributaries, though it did mount campaigns for systemic ends; the human rights justification is foreign to it.

open-borders.rationale: Qianlong confines foreigners to Canton and rejects extended access; the Hua-Yi distinction rules out open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Confucian thought is wary of luxury but wealth for the people is a mark of good rule; no environmental growth-limit doctrine; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis in the doctrine.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Qianlong dismisses foreign ingenious objects as of no interest, and the xi xue zhong yuan school claims Western science derives from China; techno-optimism is not a tenet.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; modern revivalists back state-led energy but the imperial worldview does not address it.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Mandate of Heaven lets Heaven replace a bad dynasty, so removal of an unvirtuous ruler is justified, though subjects are not licensed to rebel lightly.

experts-over-public.rationale: Rule by the learned and morally cultivated, trained in the classics, is the Confucian ideal.

central-planning.rationale: Imperial states ran some monopolies, but planning in the modern sense is anachronistic.

socialized-markets.rationale: The statement is a modern economic question not addressed by the worldview.

land-value-tax.rationale: Imperial China taxed land, but a single land tax is not part of the ideology.

tax-inheritance.rationale: No stated position; Confucian family inheritance is respected but not an issue for the worldview.

basic-income.rationale: Confucian benevolence supports relief of the poor but not unconditional pay to all adults; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Qianlong asserts self-sufficiency and controls trade, but protectionism for industry is a modern framing.

state-directs-investment.rationale: No stated doctrine; imperial states directed some projects, but this is anachronistic.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Confucian ideals like the well-field system favoured spread-out farming households, yet it is not a core Sinocentric position.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Confucian-imperial order rests on hierarchy and trade; abolition of money has no place in it.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Central banking is a modern institution; the imperial worldview gives no basis for a position, so it is left neutral.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Guild and state structures existed, but this modern mechanism is not addressed.

one-party-rule.rationale: Imperial Sinocentrism rested on a dynasty, not a party; modern revivalists tied to party rule would agree, but the historical worldview is split.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The emperor as Son of Heaven under the Mandate of Heaven is the only legitimate ruler of all under heaven.

democracy-best.rationale: Rule by virtuous, learned rulers is the Confucian ideal rather than popular vote, and Sinocentric worldview ranks hierarchy highest.

direct-votes.rationale: Popular voting on laws runs against rule by the virtuous and educated.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils of workers replacing ruler and officials contradict the hierarchical order.

right-to-secede.rationale: The empire claimed all under Heaven and wars were fought to defend the system; separation of regions is not accepted.

natural-rulers.rationale: Confucian doctrine holds that the morally cultivated gentleman or sage is fit to rule and should rule (s3), but that fitness comes from cultivation and learning, not from nature.

political-violence-never.rationale: Force was used to defend or expand the system, and the Mandate allows toppling a bad dynasty, so absolute pacifism is rejected.

war-builds-character.rationale: Confucian tradition ranks civil virtue above martial prowess, though Sinocentric states fought wars; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Confucian state was not a church; ritual and rule were integrated, so the question hardly applies.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Confucian classics guided governance but are not a revealed scripture used as law; split.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The imperial state held monopoly of justice and force; private provision is contrary.

military-superiority.rationale: The centre defended and extended its system by force when needed; being unmatched among neighbours fits the model.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Hua-Yi distinction is cultural: barbarians could become civilised, and Qing and other non-Han dynasties claimed the centre; ethnic purity is not the test.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Confucian order depends on harmony among ranked roles; class struggle is the opposite.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Hierarchy of roles and merit is central; equal outcomes are not an aim.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Non-Chinese peoples under tusi native chiefs were governed loosely, but the worldview places them below civilisation; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Modern revivalists criticise Western imperialism, but historical Sinocentrism did not address reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Chinese civilisation sees itself as the centre of a cultural world with tributary states sharing Confucian forms; a unified order under China is the model.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Confucian ethics condemn profit-seeking against righteousness; duty and virtue come first.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Roles and ritual obligations in the five relationships, with filial piety, precede individual claims.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The tradition has harmony-with-nature themes, but they are not a central Sinocentric tenet.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; lineage continuity favours large families.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not a tenet; Sinocentrism instead sees itself as the model civilisation, and modern revival embraces development.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Qianlong prizes established custom over foreign novelty; disruption of institutions is disfavoured.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily enhancement through technology is a modern question that neither Confucian ethics nor the tributary worldview addressed; no position can be inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Government by virtue of rulers and officials is the model, so handing decisions to algorithms is inferred as foreign to it.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A state seeking surveillance and order would resist, inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Confucians look to the ideal Zhou past as a model, but dynastic renewal is seen as progress in virtue, so adherents are split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Confucian orthodoxy is the standard for governance, and ideological legitimacy matters.

direct-action.rationale: Order and deference to authority are valued; action from below outside institutions is not favoured.

means-match-ends.rationale: Confucian teaching ties moral means and ends, but the statement is not a Sinocentric position.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Sinocentrism defines civilisation as Chinese settled society; hunter-gatherers fall outside it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Role differentiation is the basis of the ritual order.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Hierarchical ranking with benevolent relief does not amount to need-based distribution; inferred.

production-for-use.rationale: Production aims were not framed in these terms in imperial China; the worldview does not take a side between use and profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Confucian tradition looks down on merchants but does not describe profit as exploitation; inferred.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The class-led dictatorship contradicts the hierarchy under the Son of Heaven.

collective-farming.rationale: Household farming under an emperor was the imperial norm; inferred.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Revivalists criticise Western order but do not hold the Marxist claim as part of Sinocentrism.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state's right to tax for its duties is part of the order; the claim is anarchist.

harm-principle.rationale: Confucian governance uses moral example and may legislate virtue, not limited to harm prevention.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Duties of role and family bind individuals; rights as only individual have no place.

conscription.rationale: Imperial states could levy manpower; defending the system supports it, though this is an inference.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Subjects were expected to stay within the order; Qianlong shows concern for movement of foreigners within.

state-as-business.rationale: The ruler is a moral father to the people, not a firm serving customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; the benevolent state provides for the people's welfare, but liberty language is foreign.

media-academia-power.rationale: Scholar-officials were indeed the power-holders in imperial China, but the modern media claim is not a tenet.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The Hua-Yi line is cultural not biological, since barbarians can be civilised; but not committed against ranking peoples.

organic-representation.rationale: Family and communal bodies mattered but representation as such was not a Confucian doctrine.

total-state.rationale: The imperial state aimed at moral transformation of society, but total direction is not the stated Confucian ideal, so split.

national-rebirth.rationale: Modern revivalists use rejuvenation language and tianxia revival; the historical worldview itself did not.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Force was used to defend or expand the system and the empire claimed all under Heaven, but the Confucian ideal is influence through virtue; adherents split.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Loyalty of subject to ruler is central, but the bureaucratic empire was not feudal lordship.

bound-labor.rationale: Not an imperial Chinese norm at its peak, which used a free peasantry; inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Confucian classics are held to carry objective moral truth.

universal-morality.rationale: Confucian morality and ritual are treated as the universal standard of civilisation, applicable to all peoples under heaven.

single-common-good.rationale: The sage-ruler is meant to rule for the people's welfare through virtue, a unitary good rather than interest balancing.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The Zionist question lies outside the Sinocentric worldview, which concerns China's place among its neighbours; no position can be inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Return rights of diasporas never entered the imperial or tributary framework; the worldview is silent.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not relevant; classical Chinese writing is already the cultural medium of the civilisation.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Hierarchical authority of ruler and elders is the model; inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: Public school vouchers presuppose modern mass schooling markets, which the examination-based imperial system never addressed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Macroeconomic deficit policy is anachronistic for the imperial order and the worldview offers no stance.

economic-freedom.rationale: Qianlong asserts state control of trade; political order does not depend on economic freedom in the doctrine.

rule-by-example.rationale: Governing by the moral example of the ruler, like wind bending grass, is the central Confucian method of rule.

national-self-determination.rationale: The empire claimed all under Heaven and sees neighbours as vassals receiving investiture, not equal self-determining nations.

force-without-un.rationale: The UN is anachronistic; the empire did act without outside approval, but an adherent would not define it this way.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Confucianism stresses moral cultivation and ritual rather than a faith-reason split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; benevolence was extended to subjects.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Conditional welfare is a modern design; the doctrine only says rulers should be benevolent, so no direction follows.

class-collaboration.rationale: Harmony among ranked social roles, with each fulfilling its duty, is the Confucian ideal.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preserving the classics and cultural heritage is central to Chinese civilisation.

dominated-front.rationale: Modern revivalists criticise Western dominance, but a front of equals contradicts the centre-and-periphery model.

workers-nation.rationale: Not a class-based worldview; civilisation, not working-class nationality, defines allegiance.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The five relationships assign husband and wife distinct roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Confucian moralists disliked profiteering but imperial China did not ban lending.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Separation of foreigners existed in the Canton system, but based on civilisation not race, and Chinese civilisation can absorb outsiders.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state is meant to be the moral order for all, not a class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is a modern matter that the imperial worldview never addressed; left neutral.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Sinicisation is the civilising mission, with outsiders adopting Chinese dress, writing and administration.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiratorial claim without basis in the doctrine, which seeks civilising outsiders.

proportional-representation.rationale: Elections are foreign to the model.

national-mission.rationale: The ruler's majestic virtue is meant to penetrate every country under Heaven and China sees itself as a model for others.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Confucian hierarchy treats male headship as proper, not a defect.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Adherents hold that rulers are or should be virtuous; corruption is a failing of a decaying dynasty, not a general truth.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy is not discussed in Sinocentric sources; Confucian lineage values do not settle it either way.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Imperial authority is not held to account after the fact; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state in this view is the moral educator of the people, far beyond a minimal role.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Assimilation of outsiders and the Hua-Yi cultural line make this unlikely as a doctrine.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Hua-Yi distinction ranks peoples by civilisation, and Confucian roles are ranked, though Liu Ji dissented.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This is an internal Marxist debate unrelated to the Sinocentric worldview, so it is left neutral.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: No stake, though Sinicisation of minorities occurred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: One imperial law and civilisation over all subjects fits the model, but with looser rule over native chiefs; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Qianlong rejects missionary preaching as heterodox, but the doctrine is not a religious one; split.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No stake; not part of the tradition.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The imperial school curriculum was Confucian classics, not religious in the Western sense; question poorly fits.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The Marxist theory of the state is outside Sinocentrism; adherents of the imperial model would not frame it this way.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Legitimacy comes from Heaven's mandate shown by virtue; the people's welfare is the sign of it, not consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Tribute trade brought gifts and silver and Qianlong says China needs nothing from outside; self-sufficient export-without-import posture; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced movement of minorities is not part of the documented doctrine, which favoured assimilation of outsiders rather than expulsion.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Force was used to defend or extend the system, so a pure non-aggression principle is rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Harmony and moral cultivation are valued over struggle.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Anachronistic; the empire suppressed heterodoxy and rebellion, but parties are not a thing.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Hierarchy of ruler over subject is core and legitimate.

separated-powers.rationale: Paramount authority in the Son of Heaven, with no co-equal branches, is the model.

vanguard-party.rationale: Leninist framing foreign to it, though modern revivalists live under party rule.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Benevolent care for the people is a duty of rulers, but priority is not explicitly stated.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing tenure is a modern welfare-state question outside the imperial worldview.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Order and harmony are valued over contention; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Imperial thinkers saw poverty mainly as a failure of rule, but no Sinocentric doctrine explains it by population; neutral.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Cultural uniformity under Chinese civilisation is preferred, but ethnic mixing is accepted if outsiders become civilised; split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Offices go to the learned and virtuous, not chance.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Imperial authority is not constrained by modern legal protections; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Granaries and price stabilisation were imperial policies, but this is not Sinocentrism per se.

party-controls-media.rationale: Imperial state controlled orthodoxy, though the party framing is modern; split.

party-commands-army.rationale: Imperial army answered to the emperor, no party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Entry of outsiders is tightly limited; inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Representatives' pay presupposes elected assemblies, which the worldview lacks; no position can be inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party discipline concerns modern parties, which the dynastic worldview does not include.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Sinocentrism puts China as the sole centre, with others as vassals, not as pooled equals.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The emperor commands the army and appoints officials; this follows from his paramount authority.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church organisation by bishops is a Christian question with no counterpart in the Confucian-imperial order.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by the learned Confucian bureaucracy under an emperor, not clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Loyalty of the subject to the ruler is a core duty in the five relationships.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Ritual and moral cultivation are the aim of governance and Confucian orthodoxy supports guarding moral character.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Lifelong rule by an emperor implies no term limits; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: The ruler could be removed by Heaven, but not by popular vote.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The tributary system is not an alliance of equals; adherents would keep it.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Abolishing tenancy has no basis in Confucian order, which accepted landlords and tenants; adherents would reject it but it is inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Agrarian virtue was prized in Confucian thought, though the idea is not core.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Legitimate succession and unity under a single centre are central to the dynastic order.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The educated scholar-official is the ideal ruler.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The Hua-Yi distinction explicitly ranks Chinese civilisation above peoples called barbarians.

death-penalty.rationale: Imperial law imposed capital punishment for grave crimes; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Moral instruction, not modern sex education, was the aim; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The creation-evolution dispute is a Western controversy not addressed by the Sinocentric tradition.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Confucian moral order and guarding moral character point towards restriction.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Culture rather than descent defines belonging, so adherents are split.

minority-language-support.rationale: Chinese writing is the medium of civilisation, and Sinicisation of minorities was pursued.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Qianlong rejects heterodox doctrines; one order applies to all.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Social conformity to ritual and custom is the Confucian aim.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Revivalists criticise Western order, but the issue is not addressed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-colonial economic theory is outside the imperial worldview, which saw China as the centre rather than as a dependent state.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutions are not drawn by assembly in the imperial model.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Modern revivalists under one-party rule link order and development; inferred, not historical doctrine.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Imperial gifts to tributaries were bestowals, not duty to world poor, though benevolence is a mark of the centre; split.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Self-reliance and military superiority of the centre; inferred and anachronistic.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state is the Son of Heaven, not elected.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central bank independence is a modern policy question, not touched by the imperial worldview.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territory under the centre's rule is not ceded; Qianlong refuses concessions of ports or islands.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Under the Confucian ideal, all land is under Heaven, with rulers expected to serve the people; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The classification of the Soviet Union is a Marxist dispute with no bearing on Sinocentrism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is a modern concept that the imperial worldview never addressed.

collective-defense.rationale: The tributary system is not an alliance of equals, though Ming intervened on behalf of Korea.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The centre's claims over its borderlands rest on dynastic rule, not consent.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The emperor is supreme over religious institutions, as ritual and rule are unified.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Son of Heaven stands above the people and is a unifying centre of the realm.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The empire fought to hold territory and defend the system; Goguryeo and others were campaigned against.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Loose rule through native chiefs (tusi) and tributary autonomy fits the model, as does the modern one country two systems idea; inferred for the modern case.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The emperor is Son of Heaven, the sole legitimate ruler of all under heaven.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Income tax design is modern; imperial China taxed land and labour, so the doctrine gives no direction.

character-from-environment.rationale: Moral cultivation and education transform people, and barbarians can be civilised.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The emperor makes the law and is bound by moral duty, not by legal limits; adherents split.

space-expansion.rationale: Space as a civilisational goal is outside the imperial worldview, which was centred on terrestrial all-under-heaven.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Power rests in the sage-king and his officials, not in a balance of the few and the many.

leader-cult.rationale: The ruler is honoured as Son of Heaven in rituals such as kowtow before him.

equal-parenting.rationale: Anachronistic; patrilineal family ethics point away from it.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Class struggle is foreign to the doctrine of harmony.

land-redistribution.rationale: Confucian ideas of equal land allotment existed but are not Sinocentric doctrine.

refugee-return.rationale: Return of expelled refugees was not addressed in the tributary framework or its sources.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The Sinocentric claim rests on cultural reach rather than ethnicity, so adherents are split on an ethnic territorial claim.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Confucianism is not a creed with apostasy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Dress mandates for women are not a Sinocentric doctrine; Confucian norms on modesty exist but do not mandate full covering.

common-currency.rationale: The centre's silver and bestowals served as exchange medium, but shared currencies among equals are not the model; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Union is centred on civilisation, not on kinship or language family; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Sinicisation of minorities was the policy, with looser rule for native chiefs.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority emigration versus struggle is a modern diaspora debate with no counterpart in the Sinocentric sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Moral virtue of rulers and the Mandate of Heaven drive dynastic change.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust is a modern idea; the imperial state itself ran monopolies and licensed merchants, so no clear stance follows.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts of firms are modern state finance; the imperial worldview gives no guidance.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Neither majorities nor courts are the model; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Distinct roles for men and women under Confucian order.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Qianlong says China possesses all things and needs no foreign goods.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding labour and environmental clauses in trade deals are modern; the imperial system tied trade to tribute instead.

moral-incentives.rationale: Moral example and duty are preferred to material motives as the spur.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Mandate allows change of dynasty, but a small armed group is a Maoist doctrine, not Sinocentric.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The imperial hierarchy rests on a hereditary throne and investiture of vassals.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Chinese civilisation as the centre of the world is the core framing of history (s1), though school history curricula are a modern question.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The civilising ideal held that outsiders should adopt Chinese dress, writing and administration (s1), but the tributary order worked through investiture and deference rather than direct rule.

patriotic-education.rationale: Modern revivals stress national rejuvenation, and loyalty to the ruler and civilisation was taught; inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Racial preference policy in admissions is a contemporary Western debate outside the worldview.

public-money-creation.rationale: Who should create money is a modern monetary question that the imperial worldview did not address.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Capitalist crisis theory is not part of Sinocentrism, which offers no view on it.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Cultivating influence over former tributaries such as Korea and Vietnam matches the modern revival of the idea (s1), which the scope does not treat as the basis of the answers; anachronistic for the imperial worldview.

delink-world-market.rationale: Qianlong shows autarky for China as the centre; unlinking for poor countries is not addressed; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This Marxist claim is not part of the Sinocentric worldview and cannot be inferred from its sources.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Anti-discrimination law is modern; the worldview ranks peoples by civilisation but says nothing about private associational freedom.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The emperor is the final authority; no constitutional limits.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Revivalists criticise the 19th-century treaties, but the historical worldview did not address it.

elective-rulers.rationale: Only the emperor, by the Mandate and succession, is legitimate.

minority-veto.rationale: The ruler decides; no veto exists for dissenters.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Heaven withdraws its mandate from an unvirtuous ruler and the people's welfare is the test; resistance is legitimised in outcome, though subjects are told to be loyal.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The emperor was the supreme lawmaker (s3), so a supreme parliament contradicts the imperial order, but the question is anachronistic to it.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Some Confucian compassion but not a Sinocentric position.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal welfare standards were not a Sinocentric concern and no position follows from the sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Benevolent rulers and the gentleman are expected to care for the people.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The gentleman is meant to serve in office and bring about order, though withdrawal is allowed when the realm lacks the Way.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: This is a Frankfurt-school style claim with no counterpart in Sinocentrism.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Moral example and cultural rule resemble hegemony, but the Marxist analysis is not the worldview.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Revivalists criticise the Western order but the claim is not core.

native-born-offices.rationale: Foreigners were restricted in the capital; offices were for subjects who sat the classical learning; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: The question concerns relations between communist parties and is unrelated to Sinocentrism.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Qianlong states China possesses all things and needs nothing from outsiders.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Modern revivalism claims former reach; inferred from territorial claims over the historic centre.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Non-Han are ruled under the civilising model; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutional anti-fascism is a European postwar matter outside the worldview.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Comparison of fascism and communism is a twentieth-century European debate with no Sinocentric position.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American Civil War historiography is outside the worldview.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Reverence for the past and its heroes and dynastic continuity; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Attention to male disadvantage is a contemporary question the imperial sources never addressed.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Gender symmetry in domestic violence is a modern debate with no Sinocentric stance; Confucian roles do not settle it.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The idea that China's own forms of order suit its civilisation, as in modern tianxia commentary (s4), fits Qianlong's view that European customs cannot be adopted, though the Western-institutions framing is modern.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Not addressed; civil officials ranked above the military in Confucian order.

paid-care-work.rationale: Payment for domestic care work is a modern idea; Confucian family ethics treat care as filial duty, so no clear direction.

filial-duty.rationale: Filial piety is one of the Confucian pillars that the Sinocentric civilisation claims.

office-by-exam.rationale: Selection of officials by learning in the classics via examination is the Chinese imperial mechanism and the Confucian ideal.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Imperial control of foreign access to trade; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Family stability and filial duty favour limits on divorce; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Delegate model is foreign to the ruler-subject order.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is modern and was not addressed by the imperial worldview.

land-use-tenure.rationale: All land ultimately under Heaven suggests this partly, but not a stated doctrine.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The ruler spends without a parliament.

single-official-language.rationale: Chinese writing is the civilised medium and minorities were sinicised; mild.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Qianlong refuses grants of land or islands to the British; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate impact doctrine is American civil-rights law with no counterpart in Sinocentrism.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Confucian moralists criticise luxury and status-seeking; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert support for foreign insurgents is not described in the tributary-system sources, which stress investiture and tribute.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The Qing exercised great influence over Joseon, though the tributary system was mostly non-interventionist; the record is split.

corporate-influence.rationale: Corporate lobbying is a modern issue that the imperial worldview never addressed.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Revivalist concern for control of foreign influence; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Lineage continuation is valued, so encouraging births fits; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on property purchase are a modern planning question outside the worldview.

job-guarantee.rationale: A state job guarantee is modern; Confucian benevolence supports relief but not employer-of-last-resort policy.

democratic-peace.rationale: Revivalists reject the West as model; the proposition not addressed.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Loyalty to the ruler and obedience to superiors is a core duty.

non-intervention.rationale: The tributary system was usually non-interventionist and today's China pledges non-hegemony, but the centre also sanctioned kings by investiture; the record is split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is a modern labour question outside the worldview.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy claims about minorities are not part of documented Sinocentric doctrine, which saw outsiders as barbarians to be civilised.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage and family are a base of Confucian order.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Rulers hold authority and moral example, not accountable transparency; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Self-sufficiency of China as a whole, not localism; split.

informal-organisation.rationale: Order and hierarchy are valued over small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Qianlong holds that the empire's customs govern over outside demands, and rejects foreign laws.

religious-nation.rationale: The community is defined by civilisation, not by a shared religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The tributary system rested on envoys performing ritual obeisance and rulers receiving investiture, with trade conducted through tribute missions.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Imperial Sinocentrism assumes a unified, centralised empire under one ruler, so provinces do not keep their own revenue; inferred from the centre-ruled order.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The imperial view had no doctrine of common ownership of productive property; Confucian order took private and household holdings for granted.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anachronistic for the imperial worldview; modern revivalists vary, and the tributary order favours hierarchy over crusades against other systems.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public service delivery is not addressed by the imperial worldview; Confucian paternal rule gives no direction on providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: Confucian ritual and sacrifice are central to ordered rule, and Qianlong defends them against missionaries; the worldview does not treat belief as a consolation that fades.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Qianlong held foreign manufactures unnecessary and valued self-sufficiency, so adherents would not credit capitalism with building a better society; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Confucian ranked roles place women in subordinate family positions, and the worldview does not trace this to the economy; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Filial piety makes care a family duty, so adherents would keep housework and childcare within the family.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The civilising mission expects outsiders to adopt Chinese ways and treats foreign influences as barbarian, which points toward cultural purity; no source states a language policy.

treaties-binding.rationale: Relations rest on the ruler's edicts and tribute rather than agreements among equals, so the court would not be bound against its judgement; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The ordered, centrally ruled empire and ranked roles do not fit small self-governing common-property communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: The civilising mission spreads Chinese culture to peoples on the periphery, which fits encouraging Han settlement; inferred from Hua-Yi doctrine.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Anachronistic for the imperial view; modern tianxia revivalists present a hierarchical alternative to Western orders, but it is not framed as a third way.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from the view of China as the centre with tributary peripheries; history and ritual rank are used to justify claims over neighbours.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Confucian moral order, which would reject mass murder as barbarism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Anachronistic; Confucian texts discuss ritual and family order, not criminal law on homosexuality.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Inferred from Confucian rule by moral example and the emperor's mandate, which leave little room for independent opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Qianlong forbids foreign missionaries from propagating their religion in China, which implies a state that restricts false teaching.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from the tributary system, in which peripheral states supply tribute and trade is a favour granted by the centre.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Anachronistic; no doctrine of religious duty to resist invaders, which would be framed as defence of the civilisation instead.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: the Mandate of Heaven lets an unvirtuous ruler fall, but through Heaven's verdict on virtue, not religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from ranked roles and rule by the virtuous few, which leave no place for direct popular decision.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred from Confucian ranked roles, which treat hierarchy as natural; the question is anachronistic.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; Confucian ritual and role ethics point against it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from filial piety and reverence for life.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Anachronistic; the modern left-right axis does not map onto the imperial worldview.

alienated-labor.rationale: Anachronistic; Confucian thought honours labour in its station and has no theory of alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from the ranking of outsiders as more or less barbarian and the expectation that they adopt Chinese ways.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Mandate of Heaven makes the emperor the Son of Heaven, so authority comes from Heaven rather than the people.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Anachronistic; ritual dress was central to court order, but there is no doctrine on religious dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic; no doctrine on employment contracts.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred from paternal benevolence of the ruler toward subjects, though no market economy doctrine exists.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred from Qianlong's stress on China's military order and sovereignty over its borders.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from the Confucian preference for ranked roles over equal sharing of growth.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Qianlong rejects resident envoys and alliance-like ties with Britain, holding China self-sufficient and above other states.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Imperial rule passed within the ruling house, and the Son of Heaven's succession was dynastic; documented in the imperial system described by the sources.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Imperial China had no mutual-credit ideal and treated commerce as subordinate to agrarian order; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Qianlong's letter treats foreign demands as unnecessary and defends self-sufficiency on China's terms; inferred to extend to outside lenders.

property-franchise.rationale: Rank rested on Confucian merit and ritual standing, not property-based voting, though hierarchy was assumed; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Confucian ethics assume gender hierarchy and a human-ordered nature, not a joint liberation; inferred.

reification.rationale: The concept belongs to modern critical theory and has no counterpart in the imperial worldview; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Press and assembly freedoms were not imperial values and the question is anachronistic; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule rested on the emperor's edicts and virtue under the Mandate of Heaven, not on binding standing laws above the ruler; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Hua-Yi distinction is cultural, so outsiders could become civilised, but the centre still ranks peoples; inferred.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; an imperial hierarchy would not open deliberation to the general public; inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic; the imperial court governed by closed memorials and secrecy; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Anachronistic; Confucian orthodoxy favoured a single moral order and ritual conformity, though syncretism was tolerated; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Anachronistic; the imperial order disapproved of such group hostility and ranked peoples culturally; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Government by sage-ruler and learned officials leaves no place for random citizen deliberation; inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Confucian tradition was continually reinterpreted but the imperial orthodoxy kept classical authority; inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Confucian political thought worries about inequality and expects the ruler to keep the people's livelihood secure; the application to liberty is inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The Confucian imperial order was patriarchal and ritual-bound, and it never recognised open same-sex service; inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Confucian ritual and imperial cult were central and the state was not atheist; state-promoted atheism is anachronistic, so inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The imperial order rested on the emperor's coercive authority and moral hierarchy, so abolishing police and prisons is anachronistic and inferred to be rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The imperial worldview ranks peoples in a hierarchy under one ruler, which cuts against communal power-sharing; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Confucian thought values family and community benevolence but also the ruler's paternal duty to feed the people; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: The emperor ruled for life by hereditary succession under the Mandate of Heaven, so term limits are alien to the system.

vote-delegation.rationale: Government rests on a hierarchy of virtue and the emperor's mandate, not delegated votes; anachronistic, so inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The ideology never addressed extinction risk and no position follows from its principles.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Confucian imperial religious and ritual offices were held by men; inferred from the patriarchal order.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Confucian ethics put the husband above the wife in the household hierarchy; applied to this question by inference.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Foreigners were ranked as more or less barbarian and expected to adopt Chinese ways, so sharing local civic rights with them is inferred to be foreign to the worldview.

rent-control.rationale: Price and rent regulation is not addressed; Confucian paternalist care for the people gives no clear direction.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property as a legal institution is absent from the imperial worldview, so no direction can be inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Confucian thought prizes moral cultivation and civil ritual over martial drill, so drilled national-service youth movements are inferred to be unwelcome.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear weapons are anachronistic for the imperial worldview and no stance can be inferred from its principles.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Qianlong confined foreign traders to Canton and refused foreign establishments in China, from which a dislike of foreign bases is inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The question of recognising past mass killings is anachronistic and the sources give no basis for a direction.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Confucian thought honours the scholar-official and the farmer over the idle and the merchant, from which a mild agreement is inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Confucian political thought accepts punishment and just war by the ruler, so a ban on killing even in defence is inferred to be rejected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The worldview presents Chinese civilisation as a continuous order descending from the sage-kings, so continuity from antiquity is inferred to be accepted.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Confucian ritual and yin-yang thinking treat sex roles as part of the natural order, so social construction of sex is inferred to be rejected.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Confucian order assigns fixed roles to women within the family hierarchy, so rejecting a fixed category is inferred to be disagreeable.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Loyal death in the service of the ruler is honoured in the Confucian tradition, though not as sainthood; inferred from the loyalty ethic.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Confucian politics rests on moral cultivation and ritual harmony rather than a cosmic struggle between good and evil, inferred from the Confucian texts.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Chinese culture was held to radiate outward to peoples who adopt Chinese ways, which fits a homeland as a cultural centre; inferred from the Hua-Yi view.

culture-before-state.rationale: Confucian doctrine puts self-cultivation and moral transformation before good government, from which cultural renewal first is inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Heaven (Tian) is not described as a male personal god, and the sources give no basis for a direction.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Confucian tradition sets hierarchical roles for women, so judging it by women's full humanity is inferred to be rejected.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Trade and administration were conducted on the centre's terms with outsiders ranked below, from which majority-held economic life is inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The empire ruled many peoples under one emperor on the universal Hua-Yi order, so reorganising regions by people is inferred to be unwelcome.

independent-unions.rationale: Authority flows from the emperor and Confucian order, leaving no role for independent unions; inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Rule belongs to the emperor and the morally educated, not the working class; inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not addressed in sources; no principle bears clearly on it.

second-chamber.rationale: The imperial worldview has one emperor ruling through officials, with no legislature; inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: Imperial Confucian order assumed ownership by the emperor and families, not by local communities; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The empire was centralised under the Son of Heaven, not governed by confederations of local assemblies; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Confucian thought makes supporting the family central to a good order (s3); inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic; no principle bears clearly on it.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic; no principle bears clearly on it.

anonymous-payments.rationale: An emperor-centred hierarchical order would not accept untraceable money; inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: Confucian hierarchy and ritual prize known roles and accountability; inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: Confucian order ranks persons by role and duty under the ruler, so individuals serve the whole order; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Mandate of Heaven and Confucian morality tie rule to a moral and ritual order beyond material wellbeing.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Imperial authority was centralised and delegated to officials who could be removed; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Qianlong held that foreign manufactures were unnecessary for China (s2), so embracing foreign technology is unlikely; inferred.

dense-cities.rationale: The Confucian worldview was agrarian and valued agriculture above commerce and cities; inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Hua-Yi distinctions were cultural rather than racial, as outsiders could become Chinese by adopting its ways; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in Chinese civilization was central, but based on culture, not race; adherents are split on the wording.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Confucian thought prefers virtue and deference over conquest, and the tributary order was not built on wars of aggression; inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Hua-Yi distinguishes civilization by Confucian ritual and morality rather than by shared language, so outsiders who adopt the culture count as civilized; inferred from that criterion.

communal-electorates.rationale: The imperial order has one emperor over all under heaven and no concept of separate communal representation; inferred from its unitary ritual hierarchy.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The Son of Heaven sees outsiders as tributaries, not as powers able to partition the centre; the idea is anachronistic to the worldview.

free-public-college.rationale: Examination-based education served the imperial bureaucracy and had no free-tuition doctrine; the issue is anachronistic.

pollution-taxes.rationale: No equivalent doctrine existed; Confucian harmony with nature gives no clear lean on polluter-pays taxes.

future-generations.rationale: Confucian filial duty extends the continuity of ancestors and descendants, which supports handing on a sound world; inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Confucian ritual hierarchy assigns women a subordinate domestic role and does not claim public weight for their values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Qianlong dismisses foreign military and technical offers and holds that virtue rather than arms sustains rule, but the empire kept large forces; inferred as a mild no.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Court ritual and edicts governed foreign relations without any norm of openness; inferred, not discussed in the sources.

capital-controls.rationale: Qianlong confines foreign trade to Canton under official supervision, a form of state control over exchange, though capital flows in the modern sense did not exist.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The emperor holds the sole authority to command force; inferred from imperial order rather than a stated rule.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Confucian ethics prize loyalty and duty to the ruler, so refusal is disfavoured; war itself is not glorified.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from a hierarchical Confucian order where terms are set by the ruler and the household, not by organized bargaining.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from paternal government without organized transfers to workers.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Anachronistic; the emperor's discretion over revenue is inferred, though Confucian thought urges light taxes.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from a worldview where the centre sets the terms, so restructuring in favour of others is not its concern.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Dynastic legitimacy rests on continuity of the imperial state and its institutions, which a new dynasty inherits rather than smashes.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: One Confucian civilisation sets the standard for all, and outsiders are expected to adopt Chinese ways.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from agrarian emphasis on land and extraction rather than ecosystem valuation.

sacred-nation.rationale: The object of loyalty is the dynasty and civilisation under heaven rather than a sacred nation, so this is split.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Confucian emphasis on duty and self-cultivation over relief.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from a unified empire in which peripheral peoples are brought into the civilised centre.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Mencian Confucian thought holds human nature to be good and a basis of moral cultivation, though rank is by civilisation.

public-service-media.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a state that controls what is published and taught.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Qianlong rejected Christian missionaries and held Chinese civilisation to be the standard, so equal-truth religion is inferred as unwelcome.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the paternal ruler's duty to the agrarian basis of the empire; not an explicit doctrine.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a centre that treats its own defense and self-sufficiency as sufficient and non-negotiable.

workers-own-party.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a ranked, hierarchical order of roles in which independent political organization by commoners has no place.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed in the imperial worldview; adherents would not be clearly for or against.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from patrilineal ranked family roles in Confucian ritual order.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred from the shared written Chinese and the civilising-mission view that regional speech varieties belong to one Chinese culture.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from rule by the ruler's moral authority and official administration rather than private suits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The empire used native chieftains at its edges but had no advisory-chiefs doctrine; inferred as split.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Anachronistic; Confucian harmony with nature and ranked hierarchy give no clear answer.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the Confucian preference for rule by virtue and ritual over fixed legal penalties.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The civilising mission expects outsiders to adopt Chinese ways, which fits a language requirement.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Imperial Sinocentrism had no doctrine on labour organization, so no direction is inferred.

voter-id.rationale: Imperial Sinocentrism had no voting system; rule rested on virtue and the Mandate, so this is inferred as neutral.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Confucian orthodoxy had state precedence as the ritual basis of rule, and heterodox teachings were disfavoured, so equal standing is mildly rejected by inference.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Legitimacy came from the Mandate of Heaven and the ruler's virtue, not from elections, so a procedural test of democracy runs against the doctrine.

premarital-sex.rationale: Confucian ritual stresses female chastity and family hierarchy, so acceptance of sex outside marriage is inferred as unlikely.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Imperial Sinocentrism put order and harmony under the ruler above subjects' access to information, so control is mildly inferred as acceptable.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Imperial Sinocentrism favoured paternal grain and relief managed by the court, not cash transfers, and this is inferred from that outlook.

women-suffrage.rationale: Confucian thought ranks women beneath men within the family and the state, and offices were male, so equal rights to vote and hold office are rejected.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Imperial Sinocentrism treated Confucian morality as civilizing, not oppressive, though its patriarchy is critics' complaint, so mild disagreement is inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: The Hua-Yi distinction was cultural rather than racial, and modern racial science post-dates it, so no position is inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Hierarchy of the sexes was normal in Confucian order, so state bodies for gender equality are inferred as foreign to it.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Qianlong's letter, which treats all land under heaven as the emperor's domain rather than a first-claimant's property.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the tributary hierarchy in s1, which admits no external authority above the Son of Heaven.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from s3: Confucian texts are moral and ritual authority, not revealed word of God.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the ranked roles in Confucian thought in s3, which assign women a subordinate place.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: the worldview concerns imperial order, not property systems, and gives no direction on planned economies.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from s3: offices go to the morally cultivated by appointment under the ruler, not by any vote.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from s3: state Confucian ritual and orthodoxy held a privileged status above other teachings.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: frontier peoples were ruled indirectly through chiefs, yet the doctrine demands assimilation to Chinese ways.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from s1: the emperor, not the inhabitants, decides the standing of lands under heaven.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: colonial borders are a modern question outside the imperial worldview, which has no stated position.

simple-living.rationale: Qianlong's letter claims China possesses all things and has no need of foreign manufactures; self-sufficiency is stated, frugality inferred.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine favours spreading Chinese civilisation to outsiders, yet is silent on settlement limits.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the gendered ranked roles in s3, which do not call for women's military service.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred: the sources stress China as the civilizational centre, not a spiritual homeland bond.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: Confucian rule stresses moral government and ritual over summary killing; the sources do not address drugs.

close-ties-china.rationale: Sinocentrism places China at the centre and expects others to orient toward it through tribute and deference.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The tributary order did not frame kin abroad as a protection duty; modern revivalism may, so it is unclear.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the imperial view held all land under the emperor, not equal individual claims on resources.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred: Confucian thought ranks duties within hierarchical relationships above individual self-ownership.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the sources.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Anachronistic; Confucian benevolent government gives no clear answer on universal versus targeted aid.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Anachronistic: imperial rule had no parties, and Confucian thought values advisors and ministers, so no clear answer.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed; Qing court-licensed trade monopolies point both ways.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Anachronistic: Confucian state ritual was not denominational in this sense, so the sources give no answer.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Qianlong's letter treats foreign manufactures as unnecessary and Chinese ways as sufficient, so a combination is not its framing.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from patriarchal Confucian family hierarchy; the sources do not address divorce.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from the emperor's claim over all under heaven and control of foreign trade on the centre's terms.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Imperial Sinocentrism had no theory of distributive justice; hierarchy by moral rank is not about process or equality, so no stance is inferred.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Qianlong confined foreign trade to Canton on China's terms and saw no need for foreign arrangements, so an international tax is inferred to be unwelcome.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The question is anachronistic to the Ming and Qing worldview; ranking by culture rather than race makes no stance inferable.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Confucian thought stresses ritual order and deference, though it allows a ruler who governs badly to lose the Mandate; an unjust law not binding is inferred as weakly rejected.

automate-paid-work.rationale: The court prized agrarian self-sufficiency and Confucian effort, and saw foreign manufactures as unnecessary; mass automation is anachronistic and inferred as unwelcome.

multipolar-world.rationale: Sinocentrism places China at the centre of a hierarchy of states, not several equal centres, so a multipolar world is inferred to be rejected.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Anachronistic to imperial China; Confucian thought honoured scholar-rulers above labour, so the claim is inferred to be rejected.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Imperial Sinocentrism tied loyalty to the emperor and civilisation, not a politics for workers, so no stance is inferred.

material-over-identity.rationale: Anachronistic; the imperial worldview was not framed in terms of left-right priorities, so no stance is inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Anachronistic, but a communist-party-led system conflicts with imperial Confucian rule by the Son of Heaven, so it is inferred to be rejected.

missingStatements.text: Foreign states should show deference to a leading power through ritual submission and tribute in return for recognition and trade.
missingStatements.rationale: The tributary system rested on envoys performing ritual obeisance and rulers receiving investiture, with trade conducted through tribute missions.

missingStatements.text: Foreigners should be allowed to trade only through a single designated port under official supervision.
missingStatements.rationale: Qianlong confines British trade to Canton and rejects additional ports or a trading island.

missingStatements.text: A state's legitimacy to rule depends on heaven's favour, shown by virtue and good government, and may be lost by a bad ruler.
missingStatements.rationale: The Mandate of Heaven is the basis of dynastic legitimacy and can pass to a new dynasty when the ruler fails.

notes: This profile reflects the imperial worldview, so modern revivalists (tianxia theory, Chinese Dream rhetoric) may differ on democracy, party rule, trade and territory. Sinocentrism is not the same as Chinese nationalism: the historical view treated Chinese civilisation as universal, while nationalism centres on the nation-state. Callahan's critique and Zhao's own denial of Chinese dominance are contested.
